notes.origin: interop-vector slice 3 (42fba02) blockers: pattern paint kind (STU-VEC-017/138), vector clip and mask records (STU-VEC-053), clip/mask reference on layers

design_decision.sidecar_not_variant: The brief asked for a pattern kind alongside Solid/Gradient in StudioPaint. Adding a StudioPaint variant (even with #[non_exhaustive], which is itself a breaking change) breaks exhaustive matches with no wildcard in interop-vector: src/svg_export.rs:264, src/svg_adapter.rs:2017, tests/vector_edit_roundtrip.rs:465; this lane may not edit that crate and the brief requires dependents to keep compiling. So the pattern kind is a binding of a style row in the sidecar (StudioPatternPaint) and the row keeps a valid Solid/Gradient paint as stand-in. If the lead later wants the variant, interop-vector needs three match arms and the folio change is one variant plus the same validator (coordinated round).
design_decision.no_new_struct_fields: StudioLayer/StudioMask/LayerAppearance/StudioNodeDesign/StudioAppearanceRow are unchanged, so existing literals compile; StudioVectorRecords is #[non_exhaustive] so later vector members can be added without breaking dependents
design_decision.style_rows_by_index: appearance rows carry no id and cannot gain one without breaking literal constructors (interop-vector builds StudioAppearanceRow::Fill/Stroke by literal); a binding therefore names (style_id, row index); the code that reorders rows must update bindings. Validator checks the row exists.
design_decision.transform_on_the_fill: STU-COL-196 puts the transform on the pattern fill; STU-VEC-138 lists it under the paint contract; stored on StudioPatternPaint.placement
design_decision.cycle_check: added because SVG 2 16.1.2 makes reference loops invalid and a renderer would recurse (pattern whose tile artwork paints with the pattern, clip/mask source containing its target); RenderCycle code already existed, no new Code variant

spec_gaps: STU-VEC-053 states mask mode tokens and a mask 'region' but no clip rule, no region geometry and no units: clip_rule reuses STU-VEC-110 NONZERO/EVENODD (NONE unrepresentable); region = one document-unit rectangle (minimal form of SVG mask x/y/width/height); no objectBoundingBox mode exists in the spec (caller converts, as the gradient import does)
Meaning of mask.alpha / mask.vector / mask.luminance is not specified beyond the tokens: stored only
STU-VEC-053 'use-as-mask' sibling semantics (clips the objects above it within its container) not stored; the attachment names each clipped layer explicitly
Accord has no identity prefix for hsk.studio.pattern@1 or for clips (SMSK belongs to the raster StudioMask): pattern_id/clip_id/mask_id are set-local key-grammar ids
STU-COL-195 overlap_order members are not enumerated: stored as an opaque label

STU-COL-195 'grid' vs STU-VEC-138 'tile.rectangular': read as one member (the five-member union needs it); brick_by_row/brick_by_column have UNKNOWN interchange tokens and unrecovered offset parameters

STU-COL-196 says every transform field defaults to neutral 0.0, but a 0 percent scale is not invertible and STU-VEC-138 gives pattern_scale in percent: scale_factor is explicit and must be positive, identity() uses 100; composition order of the eight parameters is not stated (stored only)
StudioPatternPlacement::Matrix is a Folio addition (exact affine for SVG patternTransform), like StudioGradient::transform; the spec has no matrix field

pattern bounds spec marks unknown (spacing, shift distance, angles) are checked for finiteness/document unit only; tile size >= 0 (hard_min 0) and scaling_factor > 0 (physical domain) are the only bounds beyond spec numbers
Raster tile-bitmap patterns (STU-RAS-161, artifact tier, three colour modes) are a different content kind and are not stored here (definition model references a layer subtree)

consumer_mapping.interop-vector: SVG <pattern> -> StudioPattern{definition} whose content_layer_id is a group layer of the converted tile children (consumer sets visible=false on the artwork layers if it does not want them drawn; Folio does not decide), tile_width/height from the tile, spacing 0, placement Matrix from patternTransform (objectBoundingBox converted to document units by the consumer); fill url(#p) fallback -> the row keeps the fallback Solid as stand-in. <clipPath> -> StudioVectorClip{source_layer_id = group of the clip shapes, clip_rule from clip-rule (a clip needs one rule for the whole source: mixed rules stay a typed loss); <mask> -> StudioVectorMask{mode from mask-type: luminance -> LUMINANCE, alpha -> ALPHA; region from x/y/width/height converted}; clip-path/mask on an element -> StudioMaskAttachment on its layer.

unverified: that a consumer should treat the row paint as stand-in rather than ignore the row (design choice; no spec clause)
Illustrator/Affinity behaviour of live-source pattern alignment and scaling (spec lists parameters only; no oracle)
